title: Explore a synthetic asynchronous lifecycle
lead: All timings, completed effects, read results, faults, snippets and references are synthetic and unverified. No runtime measurements, execution or passing tests are claimed.
changes: Compare ordered states with their concurrent-read results and completed effects
Inspect the declared window and explicit closure without inferring read visibility
Retain independent choices across Lifecycle and all earlier lenses

references.label: Synthetic scope
references.value: Fictional admission and retry flows; no source access, reference resolution or verified results.

sections.title: From acceptance to read visibility
sections.reason: A receipt does not guarantee read visibility. The declared window closes at Applied, but a lagging replica can still return no row; the read result is authored separately.

states.label: Accepted
states.happened: The valid command is acknowledged; no projection write has completed.

states.label: Published
states.happened: The valid command has entered the stream.
states.readReturns: 404 · not projected; stream publication is not a visible read.

states.label: Applied
states.happened: The consumer has committed the projection write. A completed write does not imply every replica has caught up.
states.readReturns: 200 · row on the primary, or 404 · a lagging replica may still return no row. Authored uncertainty, not a measured response.

states.label: Visible
states.happened: The synthetic reader has observed the row. Literal </script><script>not executable</script> and <effect> text remain local claims.
states.readReturns: 200 · row visible. Literal https://example.invalid/read is text, not a request. sections.title: If the admission guard disappears
sections.reason: Select an authored fault; inspect the selected node below the argument. Diagram hover only inspects relationships.

diagram.source:
flowchart LR
A[Receive] --> N[Normalize]
N --> V[Validate]
V -->|publish| P[Publish]
V -->|reject| R[Respond]
P --> R
diagram.description: Synthetic handler flow. Receive is an ordinary non-fault node; normalization, validation, publication and response each have a distinct authored fault.

faults.title: Skip normalization
faults.breaks: Equivalent caller names can enter different buckets in this authored hypothesis.
faults.becomes: 202 accepted → 409 conflict for a name that differs only in whitespace.
faults.brokenRule: Normalize the name before comparing its identity.

faults.title: Remove validation
faults.breaks: Invalid commands enter the stream and become the consumer’s problem (synthetic claim).
faults.becomes: 400 → 202: caller sees acceptance instead of rejection.

faults.title: Lose publication acknowledgement
faults.breaks: The caller receives no receipt after publication; its retry may duplicate an accepted command.
faults.becomes: 202 receipt → unknown outcome: no response, not proof of failed publication.
faults.brokenRule: Describe an unknown response truthfully; do not turn it into a verified rejection.

faults.title: Return literal </script><script>not executable</script> and <response> markup with a deliberately long synthetic caller-facing explanation that wraps without hiding any part of the selected counterfactual argument
faults.breaks: The authored response message exposes literal <response> text rather than the intended label. This is a display hypothesis, not an executed failure.
faults.becomes: 202 accepted → 202 with text "</script>" and https://example.invalid/ (literal, not a link).
faults.brokenRule: Keep caller-facing labels readable. sections.reason: initialFault is omitted, so the first supplied fault starts selected. Change it independently of the admission section.

diagram.source:
flowchart LR
I[Receive retry] --> D[Deduplicate]
D --> S[Store receipt]
S --> O[Return receipt]
diagram.description: Synthetic retry flow with ordinary receive and return nodes, plus two independent fault choices.

faults.title: Skip deduplication
faults.breaks: A repeated request can publish twice in the authored hypothesis.
faults.brokenRule: Reuse the existing receipt for an exact retry.

faults.title: Forget the receipt
faults.breaks: A caller cannot correlate a later retry with the original acceptance.
faults.becomes: 202 stable receipt → 202 without a stable receipt identifier.

sections.title: Implementing code
sections.reason: Inspect why each curated hunk matters, without treating curation as the entire change.

entries.title: Normalize the request
entries.why: The synthetic check consumes a normalized name.

entries.title: Reject before publication
entries.why: This synthetic guard rejects an empty name before the first publish. A marker-only addition preserves an empty code body.

entries.title: Remove late validation
entries.why: The fictional consumer no longer owns the admission check.

entries.title: Keep literal display text
entries.hunk: +const literal = "</script><script>not executable</script>";+const note = "https://example.invalid/ is text, not a link";+const explanation = "synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; synthetic context; ";++literalMarker;+-literalMinus;+@literalAnnotation;
entries.why: Literal markup, URL-like text and long source rows remain local text, with no source request.
